findings.description: The Lambda function has static AWS access key and secret key values hardcoded in its environment variables. These plaintext credentials are stored in Terraform state, readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, and cannot be rotated without redeploying; they should be replaced with an IAM execution role and runtime secret retrieval (e.g. Secrets Manager).

The Lambda execution role has no attached policy, permissions boundary, or inline policy defined, meaning its effective permissions depend entirely on other configuration; if an overly broad policy is attached elsewhere the function inherits it. At minimum the role should scope permissions explicitly to what the function needs.
The function uses runtime nodejs12.x, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches, leaving known vulnerabilities unpatched in the execution environment.
